concepts.name: sequence transduction models
concepts.definition: Models that map an input symbol sequence to an output symbol sequence, such as in machine translation.

concepts.name: recurrent neural networks
concepts.definition: Sequential sequence models, including LSTMs and gated recurrent networks, that compute hidden states position by position.

concepts.name: convolutional sequence models
concepts.definition: Sequence models such as ByteNet and ConvS2S that use convolutional layers to compute hidden representations in parallel.

concepts.name: attention mechanism
concepts.definition: A mechanism that relates positions by weighting values according to compatibility between queries and keys.

concepts.name: Transformer architecture
concepts.definition: The paper's encoder-decoder architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms, without recurrence or convolution.

concepts.name: encoder-decoder structure
concepts.definition: A sequence transduction pattern where an encoder maps inputs to continuous representations and a decoder generates outputs from them.

concepts.name: encoder stack
concepts.definition: Six identical Transformer encoder layers, each containing multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network.

concepts.name: decoder stack
concepts.definition: Six identical Transformer decoder layers with masked self-attention, encoder-decoder attention, and a feed-forward network.

concepts.name: autoregressive decoding
concepts.definition: Generating the output sequence one symbol at a time while using previously generated symbols as input for the next prediction.

concepts.name: self-attention
concepts.definition: Attention relating different positions within the same sequence to compute that sequence's representation.

concepts.name: multi-head attention
concepts.definition: Attention performed in parallel over multiple learned projections, with head outputs concatenated and projected.

concepts.name: scaled dot-product attention
concepts.definition: The paper's attention function: softmax(QK^T divided by sqrt(dk)) multiplied by V.

concepts.name: queries, keys, and values
concepts.definition: Vectors used by attention, where a query is compared with keys to weight corresponding values.

concepts.name: attention weights
concepts.definition: Softmax-normalized weights assigned to values according to query-key compatibility.

concepts.name: dot-product scaling
concepts.definition: Division by sqrt(dk) to prevent large dot products from pushing softmax into very small-gradient regions.

concepts.name: attention heads
concepts.definition: Parallel attention layers in multi-head attention that can learn different relationships or representation subspaces.

concepts.name: encoder-decoder attention
concepts.definition: Decoder attention whose queries come from the decoder and whose keys and values come from encoder outputs.

concepts.name: masked decoder self-attention
concepts.definition: Decoder self-attention that blocks attention to subsequent output positions to preserve autoregressive prediction.

concepts.name: position-wise feed-forward network
concepts.definition: A two-layer fully connected network with ReLU applied separately and identically to each sequence position.

concepts.name: residual connections
concepts.definition: Connections that add a sub-layer's input to its output before layer normalization.

concepts.name: layer normalization
concepts.definition: Normalization applied after adding each sub-layer output to its residual input.

concepts.name: model dimension dmodel
concepts.definition: The shared vector dimensionality of Transformer embeddings and sub-layer outputs, 512 in the base model.

concepts.name: embeddings and softmax
concepts.definition: Learned token embeddings map tokens to dmodel vectors, while a linear layer plus softmax predicts next-token probabilities.

concepts.name: weight sharing
concepts.definition: Use of the same weight matrix for input embeddings, output embeddings, and the pre-softmax linear transformation.

concepts.name: positional encoding
concepts.definition: Information added to token embeddings so a non-recurrent, non-convolutional model can use token order.

concepts.name: sinusoidal positional encoding
concepts.definition: Fixed sine and cosine positional encodings with wavelengths forming a geometric progression.

concepts.name: learned positional embeddings
concepts.definition: Learned alternatives to sinusoidal positional encodings that produced nearly identical results in the paper's experiment.

concepts.name: computational complexity per layer
concepts.definition: The asymptotic amount of computation required by a layer type as a function of sequence length and representation dimension.

concepts.name: parallelization
concepts.definition: Ability to compute across sequence positions simultaneously rather than with many sequential operations.

concepts.name: maximum path length
concepts.definition: The longest path signals must traverse between positions, used to compare ease of learning long-range dependencies.

concepts.name: long-range dependencies
concepts.definition: Relationships between distant sequence positions that the model must learn and propagate through its computation graph.

concepts.name: restricted self-attention
concepts.definition: A proposed efficiency variant where each position attends only to a neighborhood of size r.

concepts.name: training data and batching
concepts.definition: The WMT datasets, tokenization schemes, vocabularies, and approximate-length batches used for training.

concepts.name: Adam optimizer and learning-rate schedule
concepts.definition: Training used Adam with specified betas and a warmup followed by inverse-square-root learning-rate decay.

concepts.name: dropout regularization
concepts.definition: Dropout applied to sub-layer outputs and to summed embeddings plus positional encodings to reduce overfitting.

concepts.name: label smoothing
concepts.definition: A training regularizer that makes target labels less certain, improving accuracy and BLEU despite hurting perplexity.

concepts.name: BLEU score
concepts.definition: The translation quality metric used to compare Transformer models against previous systems.

concepts.name: machine translation results
concepts.definition: The reported WMT 2014 English-German and English-French performance of the Transformer models.

concepts.name: training cost in FLOPs
concepts.definition: The estimated floating-point operations used to train models, used to compare efficiency.

concepts.name: model variations and ablation
concepts.definition: Experiments varying Transformer components and hyperparameters to assess their importance.

concepts.name: number of attention heads
concepts.definition: The hyperparameter h controlling how many parallel attention heads are used.

concepts.name: key and value dimensions
concepts.definition: The dimensions dk and dv used for projected keys and values in attention heads.

concepts.name: beam search and checkpoint averaging
concepts.definition: Inference and model selection procedures using averaged checkpoints, beam size, and length penalty.

concepts.name: English constituency parsing
concepts.definition: An additional task used to test whether the Transformer generalizes beyond translation.

concepts.name: semi-supervised parsing setting
concepts.definition: A parsing experiment using larger high-confidence and BerkeleyParser corpora in addition to WSJ data.

concepts.name: attention visualizations and interpretability
concepts.definition: Appendix examples showing attention heads tracking long-distance, anaphoric, and structural sentence relations.

concepts.name: future work for attention-based models
concepts.definition: Planned extensions to other modalities, local restricted attention, and less sequential generation.

connections.teaching_reason: The paper introduces encoder-decoder models as the standard structure for sequence transduction.
RNNs are described as inherently sequential, unlike the more parallel Transformer.
The Transformer is positioned against convolutional alternatives that reduce but do not eliminate certain path-length costs.
The main architectural claim is that attention alone can support the model.
The Transformer retains the encoder-decoder structure while changing the layer types.
Self-attention is the core replacement for recurrence and convolution in the Transformer.
Both encoder and decoder stacks use multi-head attention sub-layers.
The encoder stack is the encoder half of the architecture.
The decoder stack is the decoder half of the architecture.
The decoder generates output one element at a time from previous outputs.
Attention is defined in terms of queries, keys, and values.
Query-key compatibility determines the weights placed on values.
Scaled dot-product attention computes its output through softmax weights over values.
The scale factor is what distinguishes the paper's dot-product attention from unscaled dot-product attention.
Scaling keeps softmax from entering low-gradient regions when key dimensions are large.
Each head applies scaled dot-product attention to projected Q, K, and V.
Multi-head attention consists of multiple parallel heads.
The visualizations show heads attending to distant dependencies such as 'making ... more difficult'.
Encoder layers use self-attention so each input position can attend to all positions in the previous encoder layer.
The decoder uses masked self-attention to prevent access to future positions.
The decoder includes attention over the encoder stack outputs.
Masking illegal future connections preserves the autoregressive property.
Encoder-decoder attention takes keys and values from the encoder output.
Every encoder layer has a feed-forward sub-layer after attention.
Every decoder layer has a feed-forward sub-layer after its attention sub-layers.
The paper defines sub-layer output as LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)).
All sub-layers output the same dimension to make residual addition possible.
Embeddings and positional encodings share dmodel so their vectors can be summed and processed.
The model shares the embedding and pre-softmax matrices.
Because the Transformer lacks recurrence and convolution, positional encodings inject order information.
The paper's main positional encoding is sinusoidal.
Learned positional embeddings are tested as an alternative.
The authors hypothesize sinusoids help the model learn relative-position attention.
Self-attention avoids sequence-aligned recurrence and therefore reduces required sequential operations.
A self-attention layer connects all positions with constant maximum path length.
Shorter paths are argued to make long-range dependencies easier to learn.
The paper compares self-attention's O(n^2 d) complexity with recurrent and convolutional alternatives.
Table 1 includes recurrent complexity and sequential operations.
Table 1 and the following text compare convolutional layers with attention and recurrence.
Restricting attention to a neighborhood reduces cost for very long sequences.
Restricted self-attention lowers computation but increases maximum path length to O(n/r).
The WMT datasets and batching regime underpin the reported translation results.
The optimizer and schedule are part of the training regime used for translation models.
Dropout is both a training method and a varied component in the ablation table.
The paper states label smoothing improves accuracy and BLEU score.
Reported results use checkpoint averaging and beam-search inference settings.
BLEU is the central metric reported for WMT translation quality.
The results compare both quality and training cost against prior systems.
The Transformer is evaluated primarily on WMT machine translation tasks.
Rows A vary the number of attention heads.
Rows A and B vary key and value dimensions.
Rows C vary model width and feed-forward dimensions.
Row E compares learned positional embeddings with sinusoidal encodings.
The head count h is a defining hyperparameter of multi-head attention.
The key dimension dk appears in the scaled attention formula and head projections.
The paper tests the Transformer on English constituency parsing to examine generalization.
The semi-supervised setting provides additional parsing training data and produces the best reported Transformer parsing result.
The appendix visualizes individual heads and their apparent roles.
The interpretability examples are encoder self-attention maps.
Figure 3 shows attention following a long-distance dependency.
The conclusion names local restricted attention as a future direction for large inputs and outputs.
